title: RAW UNREVIEWED: f72 prose relates two repeated label classes rather than listing them
summary: GDT793 fixes f72's outer ring with okal twice and okaly twice and one later prose occurrence of each; the four ambiguous individual assignments and strict ordinal cycle are retained as counterexamples. The independently visible contrast is two repeated inscription classes on one ring. A complete reading of the owning prose could express a directed relation between the two classes, whereas a catalogue reading merely mentions both. Predeclare the exact full prose and one relation-bearing span before interpretation; require the same class-level role for both copies of each label and an additional written relation whose direction changes the whole reading. If the copies lack distinct visual owners or no relation span is independently justified, stop at the existing C0 entry-code account. No okal prefix/suffix value is exported.

design.mechanism: a prose relation may take two visually repeated whole-label classes as its arguments
design.unit: complete corrected f72 outer-ring label sequence and its complete later prose record
design.contrast: directed class-to-class assertion versus a flat mention of two entry codes
design.prediction: the relational reading retains two instances per class and locates a stable overt relation with direction in the whole prose; no distinct owner or extra relation span yields no capacity
